attack.justification: The fixture demonstrates a chmod command granting executable permission.

detections.behavior: Correlates a chmod argument path with a later executable image path
limitations: The rule observes permission-change and execution commands, not the filesystem mode transition itself.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: File made executable under a world-writable directory then executed

attack.justification: The positive fixture demonstrates a file utility targeting the Linux syslog file.

detections.behavior: Detects common file utilities targeting the Linux syslog file
limitations: Process arguments show intent to alter syslog but do not prove that the file changed.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Linux system log clearing via utility

attack.justification: The positive fixture demonstrates copying the Linux shadow path into a temporary directory.

detections.behavior: Detects cp commands combining a temporary path with passwd or shadow
limitations: Process arguments do not prove that the source was read or the destination was written.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Credential file copied through a temporary path

attack.justification: The fixture demonstrates a process argument naming the Linux shadow file.

detections.behavior: Detects credential-store path text in a non-allowlisted process argument
limitations: An argv reference does not prove that the named credential file was opened or read.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Credential-store path referenced in an unexpected process argument

attack.justification: The fixture demonstrates a Unix shell interpreting a fetch pipeline.

detections.behavior: Detects a bounded remote-fetch pipeline in a shell argument
limitations: Command-line syntax does not prove that a transfer completed or that downloaded bytes executed.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Remote payload piped directly to a shell

attack.justification: The positive fixture demonstrates env invoking an explicit Unix shell path.

detections.behavior: Detects the env utility invoking a common Unix shell
limitations: The rule cannot determine whether env was used to bypass a restricted execution policy.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Shell invoked through env

attack.justification: The positive sequence includes an authoritative Unix shell execution.

detections.behavior: Correlates fetch and shell exec events under one exact parent process
limitations: Shared exact parent identity narrows the sequence but does not prove downloaded content entered the shell.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Remote fetch followed by shell execution in one process lineage

attack.justification: The positive fixture demonstrates a deletion utility targeting a shell command-history file.

detections.behavior: Detects deletion utilities targeting common shell history files
limitations: Process arguments show deletion intent but do not prove that a history file existed or was removed.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Shell history file deletion

attack.justification: The positive fixture demonstrates netcat configured to execute an explicit Unix shell.

detections.behavior: Detects netcat variants using an execute flag with a common Unix shell
limitations: Process arguments do not prove that a remote connection succeeded or that the shell accepted commands.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Netcat shell execution

attack.justification: The positive fixture demonstrates inline Python requesting execution of an explicit Unix shell.

detections.behavior: Detects inline Python code calling os.system with a common Unix shell
limitations: Versioned interpreter paths such as python3.12 are outside this bounded selector.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Inline Python spawns a shell through os.system

attack.justification: The fetch process has an exact shell parent and the sequence executes the staged path.

detections.behavior: Correlates a shell-spawned download tool naming a world-writable output path, an attributed outbound TCP connection on the same host and boot, and the later execution of that exact path
limitations: The connection is bound by host and boot window rather than exact process identity.
The output argument and exact execution path do not prove which bytes were written.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Shell-spawned fetch, an attributed outbound connection, then execution of the fetched path

attack.justification: The fixture demonstrates an authoritative Unix shell execution.

detections.behavior: Detects an exact web-server parent lineage followed by a shell image
limitations: Web-server parentage plus a shell does not by itself prove exploitation or a persistent web shell.
nonClaims: Does not by itself prove malicious intent or authorize automatic response.
detections.title: Shell spawned by a web server process
